reasoning: Recent polling makes the 2026 Arkansas Senate race look unexpectedly competitive, with one high-quality public poll showing Democrat Hallie Shoffner narrowly ahead, a campaign poll showing Republican Sen. Tom Cotton slightly ahead, and at least one additional pollster and a prediction market characterizing Cotton as the overall favorite. Taken together, the freshest public data in the last 45 days points to a very small effective Senate margin of about D+1–2 in current polling, but with Republicans structurally favored in a strongly Republican state (R+16 PVI) and several analysts still expecting Cotton to win. There is no new, Arkansas-specific 2026 presidential general-election polling in the retrieved material, so no current presidential margin can be reliably stated beyond the state’s strong Republican baseline from 2024 and its R+16 PVI.

sources.name: Hallie Shoffner campaign / 2040 Strategy Group
sources.details: A 2040 Strategy Group poll for Hallie Shoffner’s campaign found Tom Cotton at 46% and Shoffner at 43%, a 3-point Cotton lead within a ±4-point margin of error, with 12% undecided, describing the race as a statistical tie.

sources.name: Arkansas Times
sources.details: Arkansas Times coverage of the 2040 Strategy Group poll emphasizes that Shoffner is "statistically tied" with Cotton, citing topline numbers of Cotton 46% to Shoffner 43% with a 4-point margin of error and noting Shoffner’s strong support among Democrats and independents.

sources.name: Talk Business & Politics / Hendrix College (via KARK)
sources.details: A Talk Business & Politics–Hendrix College poll of 1,217 likely voters found Hallie Shoffner at 47.4% and Tom Cotton at 44%, with Libertarian Jeff Wadlin at about 3% and 5.6% undecided, giving Shoffner a 3.4-point lead within a ±4.7-point margin of error and describing the race as a slight Shoffner lead.

sources.name: Yahoo News (reporting Talk Business & Politics–Hendrix College)
sources.details: A national news analysis piece reports that a Talk Business & Politics–Hendrix College text-message poll of 1,217 likely Arkansas voters found Shoffner leading Cotton 47.4% to 44%, with Wadlin at 3% and 5.6% undecided, characterizing the result as a narrow but noteworthy Democratic edge in a very red state.

sources.name: J.L. Partners (reported by Washington Examiner)
sources.details: A J.L. Partners likely-voter poll of 803 Arkansas voters for the 2026 Senate race is summarized as showing Tom Cotton with 51% and Shoffner with 35%, a 16-point Cotton lead, indicating a strong Republican advantage in that single survey.

sources.name: Octagon Elections Prediction Market Odds
sources.details: A prediction-market analysis notes that the July 25 2040 Strategy Group poll shows Cotton leading Shoffner 46% to 43% (R+3.0) and that current polling averages give Cotton an approximate R+10.2 lead (50.3% to 40.1%), aligning with betting-market expectations that Cotton is favored to win the Senate race.

sources.name: Talk Business & Politics / Hendrix College (Trump job approval)
sources.details: A statewide Talk Business & Politics–Hendrix College poll of 1,217 likely Arkansas voters finds Donald Trump’s job approval at 46% and disapproval at 53%, with higher disapproval on the economy and foreign policy; the article notes that this erosion in approval is beginning to weigh on Republican candidates in Arkansas, though it does not provide a 2026 presidential matchup.

sources.name: MAGA Report Cards (compiling official 2024 results)
sources.details: A state politics metrics site notes that in the 2024 presidential election, Donald Trump won Arkansas with 64.2% of the vote to Kamala Harris’s 33.6%, a 30.6-point margin, underscoring the state’s strong recent Republican tilt in presidential contests.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – 2026 Cook Partisan Voting Index
sources.details: A Cook Political Report 2026 PVI update indicates that Arkansas’s statewide partisan lean is R+16, establishing that Republicans hold a structural advantage of about 16 percentage points relative to the national popular vote in recent presidential elections.

sources.name: Ballotpedia – United States Senate election in Arkansas, 2026
sources.details: The 2026 Arkansas U.S. Senate election overview page summarizes the candidates and basic race information but does not itself provide polling numbers or a qualitative race rating, functioning mainly as neutral background.
